payload.selection_rationale: One proposal (practice), taken as core. It matches the measured tree. Every scanner path open (root, subfolder, SizeProbe) funnels through SynchronousIoCancel.Open (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:347-382), and that method sets no error mode. SizeProbe ran on 14 worker threads, none of them the root's, so a scope at thread entry would need one site per worker. The scope has to be per call. The spike also measured the testhost process mode at 0x8003 in 4 of 4 runs, so only the thread mode is observable. The repro test already reads the thread mode from the AfterCall hook, so a thread-scoped guard inside Open is what turns it green. The design is small: one struct scope nested in Kernel32, one `using` in Open, TryGetVolumeUsed refactored onto the scope, and one restore Fact. Practice raised no over-engineering flag. The proposal's process-wide SetErrorMode alternative is rejected for the reasons in key_decisions. I made three changes. (1) I add one architecture rule, that a path open goes only through Open, because the design's central invariant otherwise has nothing that can fail. (2) I mark the proposal's 'a SetThreadErrorMode pair is only a TEB write, no syscall' as unmeasured, and turn per-open cost into a decidable question. (3) I add cases for the shapes the code branches on: subfolder, failed open, cancelled open, pooled-thread leak, the second CreateFile route, and the counting-rule regression. The thin bug report (title only) forced two assumptions. The box comes from CreateFileW on a path on a drive with no media. With the flag set that call returns ERROR_NOT_READY (21) into the existing failure path. No stage saw that path run on a real empty drive, and validate cannot reach one. Nothing in stack_chosen: language, runtime, xUnit and PowerShell are all already declared. No prior stage is blocking. The repro stage ran the test through eng/dotnet.ps1 (exit 1), and the build needs the same route because this machine has no machine-wide SDK 10 (Q-003).

components.name: Kernel32.CriticalErrorBoxOff scope + TurnOffCriticalErrorBox() factory
components.responsibility: The only code in src/ that calls SetThreadErrorMode. The factory sets exactly SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS and remembers the previous thread mode and whether the set succeeded. Dispose restores the previous mode, and only if the set succeeded. It is a struct, allocates nothing, never throws, and default(...).Dispose() is a no-op. It is thread-scoped only and never calls process-wide SetErrorMode. Nested scopes unwind LIFO. The P/Invoke (Kernel32.cs:191-193) and the constant (Kernel32.cs:41) stay private.
components.key_interactions: Used by SynchronousIoCancel.Open and Kernel32.TryGetVolumeUsed. Nested inside Kernel32 so the P/Invoke stays private and InteropLivesOnlyInNative is untouched.

components.name: SynchronousIoCancel.Open guard
components.responsibility: `using (Kernel32.TurnOffCriticalErrorBox())` as the outermost statement of Open. It encloses the cancel-guard bracket, both CreateFile routes (the direct call at :363 and TryOpenKeepingLastAccess at :388), the AfterCall hook at :367, and every return, throw and cancel exit. This covers the root open (Scanner.cs:174/195 → DirectoryReader.Open → OpenDirectory), every subfolder open, and SizeProbe's OpenForAttributes on whichever thread calls it.
components.key_interactions: The signature is unchanged. Scanner, DirectoryReader, SizeProbe and ProbePass.Batch.Work (per-worker cancel guard) are not edited. On an empty removable drive CreateFile returns ERROR_NOT_READY (21) into Open's existing failure path instead of blocking on the modal box.

components.name: Kernel32.TryGetVolumeUsed (refactor only)
components.responsibility: Replace the hand-rolled set/try/finally/restore at Kernel32.cs:148-167 with the shared scope, so there is exactly one SetThreadErrorMode call pair in src/. Signature, return values and the m2 semantics from SL-043 do not change.
components.key_interactions: It is a behaviour-preserving move. It is what makes the guard 'centralised' in the sense of criterion 3.

components.name: Repro test (commit as-is)
components.responsibility: TheScannersRootOpenAndSizeProbeRunWithTheCriticalErrorBoxOff is the acceptance test, and its exit 0 is the done-when. It reads GetThreadErrorMode from the AfterCall hook during guard call 1 (the root open) and during SizeProbe's open. Commit the untracked file and the TestNative.cs helpers (ThreadErrorMode, SetThreadErrorMode) unchanged.
components.key_interactions: Uses SynchronousIoCancel.AfterCall and Scans.WithGuard. It reads the thread mode only, never GetErrorMode, because the testhost process mode is already 0x8003.

components.name: Restore and leak Facts (same file)
components.responsibility: New Facts covering the cases below: restore of the caller's thread mode (presets 0x0, 0x2 and 0x1) on the success, failed-open and cancelled-open exits; no leak of bit 0x1 onto a pooled thread after concurrent probes; the second CreateFile route; and TryGetVolumeUsed after the refactor. Each Fact restores the xunit thread's own mode in a finally.
components.key_interactions: Uses the TestNative thread-mode helpers and calls SizeProbe.Probe directly on temp files. Real NTFS trees in %TEMP%, never skipped.

components.name: Rule: path opens go through SynchronousIoCancel.Open
components.responsibility: Registers the one architecture rule below in the project's existing rules registry, twinned in ArchitectureRulesTests as that registry requires. That is the only thing that can fail if someone adds a second, unguarded CreateFile.
components.lives_at: the project's existing architecture rules registry and ArchitectureRulesTests (paths not inspected here)
components.key_interactions: Per SL-069 and SL-075, the parity baselines (-ExpectFacts and the settled count) must be derived from the baseline run, never a literal. Build must run the rules-parity and harness checks after adding it.

contracts.name: Kernel32.TurnOffCriticalErrorBox() -> Kernel32.CriticalErrorBoxOff : IDisposable
contracts.auth_model: Internal to FsAnalyser.Core. No privilege needed: SetThreadErrorMode is per-thread and unprivileged.
contracts.error_cases: SetThreadErrorMode returns FALSE: the scope records not-set, Dispose skips the restore, nothing throws, and the guarded call still runs (best-effort, like the BCL's DisableMediaInsertionPrompt). default(scope).Dispose() is a no-op.
contracts.notes: Sets exactly SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS (replace, not OR) and restores the previous thread value on Dispose. Thread-scoped, so the work inside must stay on one OS thread. Open is synchronous, so this holds. Final names may follow Kernel32's local naming.

contracts.name: SynchronousIoCancel.Open (signature unchanged; new postcondition)
contracts.error_cases: On an empty removable drive CreateFile fails with ERROR_NOT_READY (21) instead of blocking on the box, and the failure goes into Open's existing failure path. Access denied, cancel and any exception restore the caller's thread mode through the `using`.
contracts.notes: For the whole of Open, including the AfterCall hook and both CreateFile routes, the calling thread's mode has bit 0x1. On every exit path the mode is the caller's value again.

contracts.name: Kernel32.TryGetVolumeUsed (unchanged contract)
contracts.notes: Refactor only. It uses the shared scope instead of its inline set/restore.

key_decisions.decision: Guard per call, inside SynchronousIoCancel.Open. Do not set the mode once at thread entry (Scanner.Run or ProbePass.Batch.Work).
key_decisions.rationale: The spike measured SizeProbe on 14 worker threads, none of them the root's. A thread-entry guard needs one site per worker and silently misses any new one, and it leaks onto reused threads. Open is the single funnel for the root, subfolder and SizeProbe opens. The per-open cost (a set and restore pair over about 2.4M opens on a C: scan) is not measured. See decidable_disagreements.

key_decisions.decision: Thread-scoped SetThreadErrorMode only. No process-wide SetErrorMode, and no App-startup call.
key_decisions.rationale: Save and restore of the process-wide mode races across concurrent scan and probe threads. A process-wide call would not turn the acceptance test green, because the test reads the thread mode. It would be invisible in testhost (process mode already 0x8003, 4 of 4 runs). It would also need interop in the App project, which has none.

key_decisions.decision: One struct scope nested in Kernel32, with SetThreadErrorMode kept private. TryGetVolumeUsed is refactored onto it.
key_decisions.rationale: This is what 'centralise' means here: one set/restore pair in src/. A struct avoids a closure allocation on a hot path that runs per open, unlike a Func<T> wrapper. Nesting in Kernel32 keeps the P/Invoke inside Native, so InteropLivesOnlyInNative is untouched.

key_decisions.decision: Set exactly SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS (replace) and restore the caller's old value. Do not OR it into the old mode.
key_decisions.rationale: This matches the BCL's DisableMediaInsertionPrompt (recalled) and what TryGetVolumeUsed does today, so the refactor changes no behaviour. The measured thread baseline is 0x0 on every thread kind, so the two forms differ only if a caller has set another bit. That bit is dropped only for the length of one CreateFile.

key_decisions.decision: The scope is the outermost statement of Open, enclosing the cancel bracket, both CreateFile routes and the AfterCall hook.
key_decisions.rationale: The acceptance test samples the mode inside AfterCall, so the scope must cover it. Being outermost also restores the mode on cancel exceptions. Build must confirm TryOpenKeepingLastAccess is reached only from Open. If another caller reaches it, that caller needs the scope too.

key_decisions.decision: Handle-based calls stay out of scope: directory listing, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandleW (AfterCall sites :107, :219, :244).
key_decisions.rationale: The slice is the empty-drive path open. Media pulled out mid-scan is a different, unmeasured case, and the scope makes it a one-line `using` later. See open_questions.

key_decisions.decision: Add one fail-able architecture rule: outside Kernel32.cs and SynchronousIoCancel.cs, no code in Core calls CreateFile or CreateFileW. This differs from the proposal, which added none.
key_decisions.rationale: The design's central invariant is 'every path open passes through Open and so through the scope'. That invariant is exactly what was missing before this slice, and nothing enforces it. The proposal's cost objection (rules-parity baselines are fragile to literal Fact counts, SL-069) is real. It is handled by deriving the baseline counts, not by leaving the seam unenforced.

key_decisions.decision: Acceptance is the thread-mode Fact in Core.Tests run through eng/dotnet.ps1, plus the new restore and leak Facts. No end-to-end empty-removable-drive check, and no Fact asserts on GetErrorMode.
key_decisions.rationale: Validate cannot reach an empty removable drive. The spike showed the thread bit is observable and discriminating in testhost, while the process mode (0x8003) cannot fail a test. Plain `dotnet` fails here (no SDK 10), so builds use eng/dotnet.ps1's repo-local bootstrap (Q-003).

key_decisions.decision: Commit the repro stage's FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs and the TestNative.cs ThreadErrorMode/SetThreadErrorMode helpers unchanged, and add the new Facts beside them.
key_decisions.rationale: The engine measured that test failing at line 72 with exit 1, which is the intended pre-fix state. Rewriting it would discard the only direct evidence of the defect.

proposals.note: The only proposal handed to this run. Kept whole (scope struct, one `using` in Open, TryGetVolumeUsed refactor, restore Fact). I added one architecture rule, a wider cases matrix, and made the per-open cost a stated unknown. No cross-domain or expert proposal was given, so nothing was compared.

payload.coherence_check: One proposal, so there was no composition between designers and nothing here has yet survived a disagreement. The reviewer should argue with this design first. I checked the proposal against the measured survey and spikes for contradictory invariants. (1) Scope placement against the test sample point: the scope is outermost in Open and AfterCall (:367) sits inside Open, so the test reads 0x1. If AfterCall were invoked from a bracket outside Open, the scope would have to move outward. The survey's line numbers say it is inside, but nobody ran it. (2) Observed state against masking: the testhost process mode is 0x8003 (spike, 4 of 4 runs) and the published exe's process and thread modes are both 0x0 (spike, 3 of 3 launches). The design only reads and sets the thread mode, so the test can fail (it did, exit 1) and the guard is needed in production. (3) Scope granularity against the spike's 14 worker threads: the per-call scope is the one placement consistent with both the 14-thread finding and the thread-only mode, so the no-go was absorbed, not overridden. (4) Error contract: the proposal says ERROR_NOT_READY (21) lands in the existing root-open failure path, the same result a user pressing Cancel on the box produced. That is recalled, and no stage exercised it, because no test can produce an empty removable drive. It is recorded as a non-material case, not asserted. (5) The proposal's claim that SetThreadErrorMode is a user-mode TEB write is recalled and I treat it as unmeasured. It may cost one to three cheap syscalls per open. That is the one place where the design's cost could disagree with reality, and it is a decidable disagreement below. (6) Seam I changed: the proposal declined any architecture rule, but the funnel invariant has no enforcement. I added one must_not_match rule, which needs a registry twin and derived, not literal, parity baselines (SL-069). No import rule is added. InteropLivesOnlyInNative already covers P/Invoke placement, and the private P/Invoke means another SetThreadErrorMode call site would not compile. Nothing else conflicts: the reused TryGetVolumeUsed semantics and the new scope share one contract (replace and restore, thread-scoped), so there are not two error contracts.

architecture_rules.name: every scanner path open goes through SynchronousIoCancel.Open, where the critical-error scope lives
architecture_rules.because: A CreateFile call made anywhere else opens a path on the drive without SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS. On an empty removable drive it raises the 'insert a disk' box from that thread. This is the defect SL-077 fixes, and it went unnoticed before because nothing tied the opens to one funnel. Build must run this rule against the tree first. If it fires on a legitimate file, for example a TryOpenKeepingLastAccess that lives elsewhere, add that file to except_files only after confirming its callers are guarded. Do not loosen the pattern.

cases.shape: whole-tree scan of a temp NTFS folder; the root's listing open is guard call 1 on the scan thread
cases.why: This is the reported bug and the repro test's first assertion. Without the scope the thread mode reads 0x0 and the box can appear on an empty removable drive.

cases.shape: a probe worker thread, and a direct SizeProbe.Probe call on the test thread, each opening a temp file with FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES
cases.why: SizeProbe runs on worker threads other than the root's (14 threads in the spike). A guard set at scan entry would miss them, and this is the repro test's second assertion.

cases.behaviour: open a nested folder during the scan
cases.shape: the tree contains a folder with a subfolder, so non-root opens run through OpenDirectory
cases.why: The retro lesson was a bug found only on folders with a subfolder. A drive can be pulled after the root open, and every non-root open is a path open that must be guarded the same way.

cases.shape: the open goes through TryOpenKeepingLastAccess (the second CreateFile at :388) instead of the direct call at :363
cases.why: Two CreateFile routes exist. If the second is reached from outside Open, or the scope does not enclose it, half the opens are unguarded and the repro test may not notice.

cases.behaviour: give the thread its mode back
cases.shape: thread mode preset to 0x0 before a direct SizeProbe.Probe, then read after it returns
cases.why: A scope that fails to restore leaves bit 0x1 on a scan or pool thread for the rest of its life. The spike's baseline was 0x0 on all threads.

cases.behaviour: give the thread its mode back
cases.shape: thread mode preset to SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX (0x2) before Probe, then read after it returns
cases.why: Replace semantics mean the caller's other bits must come back, not be cleared or OR-ed with 0x1 permanently.

cases.behaviour: give the thread its mode back
cases.shape: the caller already has SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS (0x1) set, as in a nested or already-guarded call
cases.why: Restore must return to 0x1, not clear it. A scope that always restores 'off' would break a caller that guards the whole scan.

cases.shape: the open fails (unreadable folder, access denied err 5, and a missing path), so Open takes its failure path
cases.why: The failure exit is where a restore that is not in a finally or `using` gets skipped. The counting rules already require an unreadable-folder test, so the same tree can be reused.

cases.shape: a scan cancelled while an open is in flight, so the cancel bracket throws or returns through Open
cases.why: The scope wraps the cancel bracket. Cancellation is the path that throws out of Open, and an unwound exception must still restore the thread mode.

cases.shape: several probes run concurrently on distinct worker or pool threads, then a reused pool thread reads its baseline
cases.why: The spike's 14 worker threads are reused. A thread-entry or unrestored guard leaves bit 0x1 on them, which is the failure the pattern in cross_domain_transfer is written to prevent.

cases.behaviour: TryGetVolumeUsed after moving onto the shared scope
cases.shape: a valid drive root and a non-existent drive letter, with the thread mode read before and after
cases.why: This refactor must not change the m2 fix from SL-043. Results (used bytes, false for a missing drive) and the restored mode must be identical. The bit inside GetDiskFreeSpaceEx cannot be hooked, so the test checks result equality and the restore.

cases.behaviour: counting rules through the guarded Open
cases.shape: the existing counting-rule suite (links not followed, hardlinks once, on-disk size, long paths, unreadable folders) run unchanged on real NTFS trees
cases.why: The project constraint requires those tests before any scanner slice passes. Open wraps every open, so a regression there would show up as a wrong count, not as an error-mode failure.

cases.behaviour: open a drive with no media (ERROR_NOT_READY 21 into Open's failure path)
cases.shape: an empty removable drive, and equally a whole-drive C:\ scan versus a folder scan
cases.why: Judged not worth a test. No engine stage can produce an empty removable drive, and Open does not branch on drive root versus folder. Validate cannot reach it either, which is the slice's stated reason for a thread-mode test. The spike's published-exe launch on C:\ already covers the drive-root path.

cases.behaviour: handle-based calls during the scan (listing, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandleW)
cases.shape: media removed after a handle is open and the next call on that handle hits a 'no disk' condition
cases.why: Judged out of scope. These calls take no path, and the report is about the empty-drive open. It is unmeasured, and the next slice can disagree. See open_questions.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Thread-local ambient context in logging and tracing (MDC / Activity scopes)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Scope ambient per-thread state to the unit of work, with push on enter and pop on exit via using/finally, at the one choke point every unit passes through. Do not set it at thread entry: work fans out over pooled threads, a thread-entry setting misses threads nobody remembered, and the state leaks onto reused threads.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The thread error mode is thread-local ambient state and behaves like logging context. The spike's no-go, SizeProbe on 14 worker threads and none of them the root's, is the classic 'set at thread start and miss the pool' failure. SynchronousIoCancel.Open is the choke point. This is a description of the design, not a source of extra machinery.

invariants.precondition: The work inside the scope stays on one OS thread between set and restore, with no await or thread hop inside Open.
invariants.evidence: Open brackets synchronous CreateFileW calls with a per-thread cancel guard (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:347-382). The spike read the thread bit back on the same thread in 21 of 21 readings per run.

invariants.precondition: Every path-taking native call on the scan path goes through the choke point.
invariants.evidence: Survey: every scanner open funnels through SynchronousIoCancel.Open. Spike inventory: 16 imports, and the only path-taking ones are CreateFileW (via Open) and GetDiskFreeSpaceExW (already guarded in TryGetVolumeUsed). 0 pre-root drive touches in 6 C: runs. BCL DriveInfo calls are wrapped by the BCL itself (recalled). The new architecture rule makes this fail if a second CreateFile appears.

invariants.precondition: The scope restores on every exit path, and nested scopes unwind LIFO.
invariants.evidence: The restore, failed-open, cancelled-open and caller-already-set Facts check it. By construction it rests on `using` over a struct.

invariants.precondition: The observed state (the thread mode) is not masked by an outer default in the test environment.
invariants.evidence: Spike: the thread baseline was 0x0 on every thread kind in 4 of 4 runs. Only the process mode is masked (0x8003), and no test reads it.

decidable_disagreements.question: Is the per-open cost of the scope (SetThreadErrorMode set and restore, about 2.4M opens on a C: scan) small enough to keep the guard inside Open?
decidable_disagreements.positions: Proposal: per-call scope in Open, estimated at roughly 0.1-0.2 s in total. It calls the pair a user-mode TEB write with no syscall, which is recalled, not measured. Alternative: set the mode once at scan-thread entry and at each probe worker's entry (Scanner.Run and ProbePass.Batch.Work), restoring at exit. That alternative is rejected on coverage grounds, because each new worker site can be missed. Nobody disagreed. This records the one measurable claim the placement rests on.

taste_disagreements: Architecture rule: I add one must_not_match rule (path opens only through Open) where the proposal added none, on cost grounds. The cost is a registry twin and parity baselines (SL-069, SL-075). It is a matter of taste whether a two-file fix carries that.
Replace versus OR: the scope sets exactly 0x1 (BCL and TryGetVolumeUsed semantics). OR-ing into the old mode would keep other thread bits inside the open. I kept replace for behaviour parity.
Placement of the scope type: a struct nested in Kernel32, as against a standalone Native/ helper file. Nesting keeps the P/Invoke private, and a separate file would need the P/Invoke widened.
Whether the restore Facts belong in FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs or a separate class. Same file was chosen so the test-only thread-mode helpers stay together.
open_questions: Should media removed mid-scan, so that handle-based calls (listing, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandleW) hit a 'no disk' box, be brought into scope? This slice guards only path opens. No stage measured that case, and it needs a person's call on scope.

prior_art.pattern: Set the critical-error flag just before touching a removable drive (Dir / GetVolumeInformation), then restore it, so an empty drive fails quietly instead of raising the box
Do not pre-check which drives are 'ready' (that path itself raises 'There is no disk in the drive'). Temporarily disable the prompt around the probe instead
Failure mode: a size query on a pulled removable drive raises 'no disk in the drive, please insert a disk' from inside an ordinary library call

DisableMediaInsertionPrompt: an internal disposable struct that calls SetThreadErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS, out old) and restores `old` in Dispose only if the set succeeded. It wraps each individual path-taking Win32 call (FindFirstFile, GetFileAttributesEx, DriveInfo)
SetThreadErrorMode (Windows 7+) exists because process-wide SetErrorMode save/restore races between threads. The docs also recommend process-wide SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS at startup as a best practice
